title: It was never not-good-enough
angle: The AI was never not-good-enough for this mechanic — it was too expensive. A savings ladder that re-prices the same measured tokens, rung by rung.
endline: A cost lever. Never a correctness lever.

marks.do: The $4 problem. 400,000 tokens is the arithmetic, not an anecdote.

slides.text: The AI was never not-good-enough for this mechanic. It was too expensive to use.
slides.sub: He hit the limit screen at eleven in the morning. That is not an accuracy problem — it is a *unit-economics* problem.
notes: "He doesn't use AI. Not because it's wrong — because one question cost him about four dollars, and he hit the limit before lunch."
What the judge should feel: this is a real person with a real bill, not a benchmark.
Say ~he says~. His ~$4 is his bill on his manual. Never blend it with our $12.40.

items.label: model tiering
items.sub: identify.photo $0.024661 → $0.000532 · identify.part $0.014047 → $0.000239. Tiering is per route, not per product — and *nothing* runs on the flagship.

items.sub: ask.router's 3,000-token vocabulary translator, pinned with prompt_cache_key per route+model. A big prompt is cheap when it never changes.

notes: The constraint and the fuzzy match were doing the accuracy work, so the flagship stopped earning its price. Say it that way — it is a measurement, not a preference.
The expensive tokens are the ones that change. ingest.struct is 47.0% cached over 70.4M tokens; chat.answer 42.7%; ask.picker 34.6%.
Tiering is worth 4.8× here. *Not reading the manual* is worth 48×.

*Caveat, know it before a judge opens the report.* token-company.md, openai.md and the regenerated token-company/cost-report.md all say identify.photo $0.000532 and 46× as of 2026-09-20; the mean drifts as calls are logged, so quote the route and the direction, not the decimal.

slides.title: Compression, where nothing else could reach

left.label: tokens removed before the prompt was billed
left.caption: 46,501 → 31,977 over 25 answers · 581 tokens an answer · 21.7% of the chat bill

right.label: the setting we refused
right.caption: at aggressiveness 0.5 it ate printed values and sometimes a PAGE fence. We shipped 0.3 and got the rest by deleting dealer boilerplate instead.

slides.caption: *Cutting text that carries no information beats compressing text that does.* 368/368 KTM and 256/256 BMW printed figures survive, and a lost page fence throws the whole compression away.
notes: A lost fence silently reattributes one page's text to another page's number. A lost torque figure is exactly the thing this product exists not to get wrong — *a wrong torque breaks a motorcycle, and the mechanic is liable for it.*
Quote the *31.2% eval figure* and name it. The live /cost/ttc counter is in-memory PER REPLICA and zeroes on restart, so a low number means a fresh replica, not a worse compressor. Do not say 31.4%.
Do not state what the compressor costs us: there is no public $/M, we log it as $0 and count tokens instead.

slides.title: The token path
slides.caption: Three orange boxes are the whole bill, and bear-2 is the first of them — a cost lever between the pages and the model, never a correctness lever.
notes: *The one line to say over this:* compression sits between the PDF text layer and every model call — and it is a cost lever, never a correctness lever. No key, a 5xx, a timeout, a lost page fence: all four return the original text.
Why one call and not one per page: the API allows 60 requests/minute. Per-page compression would have capped the whole product at ten chats a minute.

Then the live demo: /cost/ttc, the chat footer's "N tokens saved", tap the [p. 78] chip, reload the counter. Warm a *different* question beforehand — a repeat is served from the answer cache at $0 and the counters will not move.

Do not blend his ~$4 with our $12.40 — different measurements of different manuals.

groups.label: All nine, global
items: ElevenLabs voice is never "live" — "built, one key away". The live voice is Deepgram.
The 3D backdrop is a technical grid. No panorama, no photographic workshop scene.
Dropbox folder sync and Climate Fit are "built, deploying", not deployed.
Never quote a running ledger total without the date beside it.
Never call 13,537 "manuals" — distinct fetchable PDFs is 14,770.
There is no checkout. "Live prices", never "buy".
